title: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy
subtitle: An ancient mystery takes to the air
summary: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS puzzle adventure concluding the series' prequel trilogy. Layton, Luke and Emmy join the archaeologist Desmond Sycamore after a discovery involving a girl preserved in ice. body: Professor Layton and the Azran Legacy is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS puzzle adventure concluding the series' prequel trilogy. Layton, Luke and Emmy join the archaeologist Desmond Sycamore after a discovery involving a girl preserved in ice. Their investigation leads toward the vanished Azran civilisation and a journey aboard the airship Bostonius. The premise expands the professor's travels beyond a single town. Different destinations become parts of one archaeological question, with the familiar habit of stopping to solve a puzzle accompanying a much wider expedition.

The search for five Azran eggs sends the group to a selection of distant locations. Players investigate their inhabitants and surroundings using the touchscreen magnifying glass, revealing conversations, hint coins and puzzles. These separate destinations give each local mystery a place within the expedition's larger purpose. Travelling aboard the Bostonius connects them, allowing the adventure to move between distinct settings instead of keeping every discovery inside one enclosed community. The recurring tools remain easy to recognise even when the scenery and the immediate problem change.

The story brings together questions raised by the prequel adventures while continuing to make individual puzzles the player's regular contribution. A character may need help, an object may conceal another clue or an apparently simple task may require a different reading. The expedition provides a reason for these encounters to accumulate across a larger map. As the final prequel chapter, Azran Legacy gives Layton's earlier travels a destination, keeping Luke and Emmy alongside him while the discoveries connect personal relationships with the remains of a much older world.
